items.claim: Serialising a known local value (a PHP array) produces the exact byte-level template a tester needs in order to recognise, and later craft, a serialized object on the wire.
items.body:
Serialising a known local value (a PHP array) produces the exact byte-level template a tester needs in order to recognise, and later craft, a serialized object on the wire.

HackTricks reference: 312098c3 (notion:312098c3-95c5-800d-86de-e52ab38c4867)
items.disproof: The application never parses attacker-supplied serialized bytes, so locally generated serialization output has nothing to be matched against.

Serialized Array:

Either an array of class names which should be accepted, false to accept no classes, or true to accept all classes. If this option is defined and unserialize() encounters an object of a class that isn't to be accepted, then the object will be instantiated as __PHP_Incomplete_Class instead

items.claim: A Python target's native serialization format is pickle, so identifying the target language's own serializer is the first step in deciding what bytes a deserialization sink will accept.

items.disproof: The application's deserialization sink accepts a fixed non-serialized format such as JSON, so no native serializer output is ever consumed.
